chain_steps.what_happens: Sensors and humans generate raw observations: EO/IR and SAR imagery, full-motion video, GMTI radar, SIGINT/ESM intercepts, air-defense radar plots, acoustic, HUMINT reports, blue-force position reports, logistics status. Collection is tasked by collection managers but much is continuous (radars, SATCOM ISR, ADS-B-like tracks).
chain_steps.who_performs: ISR crews (RC-135, MQ-9, E-2D, P-8), satellite operators (NRO, SDA tracking layer, commercial EO), radar operators (Patriot/THAAD/AN-TPQ-53 crews), small-UAS operators at platoon-company (Ghost-X class), scouts/forward observers, SIGINT teams; echelons from squad to national agencies.
chain_steps.hardware: Satellites (NRO Starshield-based constellation; SDA tracking layer), aircraft sensors, ground radars (AN/TPQ-53, TPY-6), sUAS (Ghost-X named in NGC2 Ivy Sting feeds), soldier devices (ATAK end-user devices), vehicle sensors.
chain_steps.software: Sensor firmware and payload controllers; MISB KLV metadata encoders for FMV; radar plot extractors; collection management tools (e.g., within DCGS family, Maven Smart System collection views - inferred).
data_formats_protocols: STANAG 4609 / MISB ST 0601 KLV (FMV metadata) - verified via open-source parsers (paretech/klvdata, QGISFMV)
STANAG 4607 (NATO GMTI format) - verified (MITRE paper; pentlandedge/s4607)
NITF / STANAG 4545 (still imagery) - verified via codice/alliance, bradh/jim
STANAG 4658 (ESM) - single snippet only, LOW confidence
Cursor on Target (CoT) XML for sUAS/soldier reports - verified (MITRE Event.xsd v2.0, 2003)
chain_steps.human_in_loop: Sensor operators steer payloads; collection managers prioritize; FMV/GMTI mostly machine-generated, HUMINT fully human.
chain_steps.latency_sources: Sensor revisit rate, satellite downlink windows (mitigated by laser crosslinks - NRO says minutes-to-seconds), aircraft datalink availability, operator queueing.
chain_steps.comms_dependencies: Downlink/backhaul (SATCOM, CDL, line-of-sight datalinks, mesh radios) to move raw data off the sensor.
chain_steps.when_connectivity_disappears: Sensor continues recording locally (store-and-forward); tactical sensors publish to local mesh/TAK server; national/airborne ISR products become unavailable to disconnected units.
chain_steps.interoperability_requirements: Standard container/metadata formats (KLV, 4607, NITF) so downstream PED tools can ingest; CoT for tactical SA.
chain_steps.security_domain: Ranges from Unclassified/CUI (sUAS FMV) through S and TS/SCI (national ISR, SIGINT). Coalition releasability determined at collection tagging.
chain_steps.owning_organizations: NRO/NGA/NSA (national), SDA (space transport/tracking), service ISR wings (ACC ISR, Navy VP/VQ, Army MI brigades), PEO IEW&S (Army sensors), PEO Aviation; Marine MIGs.

chain_steps.who_performs: Signal/communications units (Army signal battalions, ESB, 'G6/S6'), Air Force comm squadrons, Navy combat systems/IT, DISA (DISN, MPE transport), Space Force (SATCOM, SDA), commercial SATCOM operators.
chain_steps.hardware: MIDS JTRS / Link 16 terminals (Data Link Solutions: 9,000+ delivered to 50+ nations; $248M Navy production Jan 2026), tactical radios (L3Harris, Collins, Silvus, TrellisWare - the latter two not verified in this run), SATCOM terminals (Viasat, Starshield/Starlink), TSM/MANET mesh, private 5G (named in NGC2 lead responsibilities), SDA transport satellites with laser crosslinks, Ka downlinks and Link 16 antennas, JREAP gateways.

data_formats_protocols: JREAP (MIL-STD-3011) A/B/C over serial/SATCOM/IP - verified via secondary
IP/TCP/UDP multicast (TAK default multicast 239.2.3.1:6969) - verified via secondary
MQTT/DDS as transport middleware - DDS (RTI Connext) confirmed in defense use; MQTT usage in DoD C2 not verified in this run
chain_steps.human_in_loop: Network planners build Link 16 network designs and PACE plans; operators manually re-key/re-route when links fail; largely machine-executed once configured.
chain_steps.latency_sources: Link 16 time-slot allocation and ~300 mi LOS limit (extended by JREAP with added latency), SATCOM hops (GEO ~500+ ms round trip, LEO tens of ms), gateway translation, congestion on low-bandwidth radios, jamming-induced retransmits. SDA laser mesh not yet operating cross-vendor (July 2026).
chain_steps.comms_dependencies: This IS the dependency; everything above and below assumes some transport. Spectrum availability and host-nation restrictions constrain it.
chain_steps.when_connectivity_disappears: Fallback to PACE alternates (HF, courier, runner); units revert to local mesh; store-and-forward queues; commanders act on last-known picture. PC-C6 (July 2026) reported intermittent connectivity and overheating gear - FACT (secondary reports citing Axios).
chain_steps.interoperability_requirements: Waveform and crypto commonality (Link 16, SATURN, coalition waveforms), FMN-compliant coalition transport, JREAP/SIMPLE gateways, IP everywhere.
chain_steps.security_domain: Crypto-separated enclaves by classification; Link 16 is Secret-level; coalition networks (CENTRIXS/BICES/SABRE) separately keyed.

cross_cutting_observations.observation: The Army has converged NGC2's ingest/normalize/store layers on a two-vendor baseline (Lattice tactical, Foundry cloud) plus Raft registries; every future NGC2 app is expected to run on it.
cross_cutting_observations.evidence: Army statement June 22, 2026; Palantir and Anduril releases; Raft named by MeriTalk.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT

cross_cutting_observations.observation: NGC2 cost is large and unbounded publicly: >$1B for 4ID full stack; potentially several $B per year; $3.3B identified through FY26; ~$904M FY27 RDT&E requested; no lifecycle cost estimate or unit-by-year schedule; goal 11 divisions and 4 corps by FY2032.
cross_cutting_observations.evidence: GAO report Aug 20, 2026; Military Times Aug 4, 2026.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Contract ceilings dominate headlines and must not be read as revenue: Anduril's Army enterprise agreement carries a $20B ceiling; Maven ceiling ~$1.3B through 2029; TITAN actual production obligation is $192M for 8 systems.
cross_cutting_observations.evidence: Benzinga/Anduril June 23, 2026; DefenseScoop May 2025; Military Times Sept 2, 2026.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Field results at PC-C6 (July 20-29, 2026; ~9,000-10,000 personnel, six brigades, 90+ technologies) showed 'common visualization' success but intermittent connectivity and equipment overheating; the Army's evaluation criteria include kill-chain speed, survivability, jamming effects, cognitive load and allied interoperability.
cross_cutting_observations.evidence: Secondary reports citing Axios; Business Insider July 29-30, 2026; National Defense Aug 18, 2026.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Policy, not technology, is the binding constraint on cross-service and coalition data sharing, per GAO (overly restrictive classification) and an industry panelist at AFA 2026 ('not actually a technological impediment... policy impediments').
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Fire-control-grade fusion remains a separate, hardware-coupled world (IBCS in full-rate production since Nov 2025, Aegis, Link 16) from the software COP world; Link 16 and C2BMC are described by FDD as purpose-built workarounds rather than unified C2.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Space transport is arriving but late: SDA Tranche 1 Transport had 63/126 satellites on orbit by July 16, 2026 after a months-long pause; cross-vendor laser mesh not yet demonstrated; SpaceX won a $2.29B LEO backbone award (May 2026).
cross_cutting_observations.evidence: SpaceNews July 16 and May 26, 2026; Tech Times July 14, 2026.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Autonomy C2 is a demonstrated failure point: Replicator delivered hundreds, not thousands, of systems by Aug 2025, hobbled partly by software unable to command large heterogeneous drone sets; DIU issued C2/ACT software prototype awards to seven companies (Nov 2024).
cross_cutting_observations.evidence: Tech Times citing CRS, July 16, 2026; Aviation Today Sept 4, 2025.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT (secondary)

cross_cutting_observations.observation: The app layer on the new data platforms is where non-prime startups are visibly winning slots: Onebrief (planning), Air (sustainment), Striveworks (MLOps), Govini, Rune, RII, Instant Connect, Ditto (DDIL sync, USMC).
cross_cutting_observations.evidence: Vendor releases June-July 2026 naming NGC2 partner sets.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT (vendor-stated participation; contract values undisclosed)

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Anduril publishes Lattice SDKs in six languages (since Aug 2024) with an entity model including MIL-STD-2525C and mil_view.disposition overrides, and an AI-skills repo (July 2026); technical openness of the API is real, but commercial terms, data rights and government-side licensing are not public.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT + INFERENCE

cross_cutting_observations.observation: TAK/CoT is a government-owned, open de facto standard with a large OSS ecosystem (TAK Server, FreeTAKServer, OpenTAKServer, pytak, Meshtastic ATAK plugin), which lowers barriers for SA integrations but also commoditizes the COP layer.
cross_cutting_observations.evidence: GitHub star counts Sept 2026; TAK protobuf verified.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Maven is positioning as the joint developer platform (25,000 builders; a program of record chose to run on Maven) and DoD directed component transition on an aggressive timeline; Palantir's DoW TTM revenue is still <25 bps of the Pentagon budget.
cross_cutting_observations.evidence: Palantir Q2 2026 earnings call Aug 3, 2026; DefenseScoop Apr 15, 2026.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT (company statements)

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Two divergent prototype stacks (Lockheed/25ID vs Anduril/4ID) forced the Army to declare a common baseline within a year; app portability and cross-stack data sharing were the real pain, and the Army now explicitly wants divisions to 'reuse applications'.
cross_cutting_observations.label: INFERENCE

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Sensor-to-shooter timelines are quoted in vendor materials (under one minute for 26 M777 missions; 'minutes to seconds') but no independent, exercise-published measurement was found; treat as unverified.
cross_cutting_observations.label: HYPOTHESIS (vendor-claimed)

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Assessment (ASSESS) is the weakest step publicly: no named systems, GAO says DoD cannot measure CJADC2 progress, and lessons-learned sharing is limited.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT

cross_cutting_observations.observation: The DAF side is converging on the same pattern: PAE C3BM owns the DAF Battle Network; CBC2 fusion vendor (SciTec) selected; TOC-L MR2 kits due by end 2026; DASH sprints test human-machine teaming and then transition to classified networks.
cross_cutting_observations.evidence: af.mil Sept 8 and Aug 24, 2026; Air & Space Forces Magazine Sept 22, 2026; Firefly Q2 2026 call.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT

cross_cutting_observations.observation: Allied markets are deliberately multi-vendor: NATO NCIA reportedly selected Palantir, Anduril and Athea for next-gen air C2 (July 2026) 'to avoid dependence on a specific supplier'; Thales launched HexaForce (Sept 2026) with FMN/DCS.
cross_cutting_observations.label: FACT (LOW confidence on NCIA details)

where_value_is_moving: From monolithic programs of record (CPCE, DCGS-A, AFATDS-era) toward a commercially owned two-layer data platform (Lattice edge + Foundry cloud, Maven at joint level) with an app ecosystem on top. Value is moving (1) up into warfighting-function apps and workflows on those platforms (planning, sustainment, fires, airspace, C-UAS), (2) down into DDIL-tolerant sync, transport-agnostic networking and edge compute hardware integration (TITAN shelters, TOC-L kits), (3) sideways into data-centric security/releasability for coalition and cross-domain (policy-bound but underserved), (4) into test/instrumentation, EW emulation and human-machine-teaming evaluation, and (5) into commercial LEO transport (Starshield/MILNET, SDA). The platform layer itself is consolidating under enterprise agreements with very large ceilings (not obligations), which shrinks greenfield for new middleware startups but raises the number of integration points that need third-party software.

keep: tactical comms (with the split noted below)

change.recommendation: Split into (a) planning/collaboration/workflow apps, (b) execution apps by warfighting function (fires, airspace, protection, sustainment) that run on the data layer, and (c) fire-control C2 (IBCS/Aegis class) as a separate, hardware-coupled sub-segment.
change.why: Evidence shows very different buyers, certification regimes and incumbents: Onebrief-type planning apps enter via OTA partner sets; fire control is in full-rate production under primes with safety certification; lumping them hides the accessible part.

change.recommendation: Rename to 'data layer and adjacent services' and scope to registries, schema transformation, federation, DDIL sync and cross-stack app portability - not new core platforms.
change.why: The core platform decision has been made for Army (Lattice/Foundry, June 2026) and joint (Maven directed transition, Apr 2026); the surviving startup space is services around those platforms (Raft, Ditto).

change.recommendation: Split into 'enterprise PED' (Maven/NGA) and 'edge PED/targeting nodes' (TITAN, TOC-L), and treat edge PED jointly with 'edge compute/AI'.
change.why: TITAN production (Sept 2026) shows edge PED is now a hardware-plus-software integration market distinct from enterprise analytics.

change.recommendation: Separate 'track management/fusion' (belongs with FUSE; fire-control-adjacent, Link 16/IBCS) from 'geospatial SA/COP' (commoditized by TAK and platform UIs).
change.why: They have different technical difficulty, buyers and standards (STANAG 4676/Link 16 vs CoT/2525).

change.recommendation: Treat as cross-cutting requirement plus a concrete product category: releasability labeling, data-centric security, FMN gateways and translators; merge governance with identity/zero-trust/cross-domain into 'data-centric security and releasability'.
change.why: GAO and AFA panel evidence shows the blocker is policy/labeling, which is where tooling can help; pure 'interop' is not a product.

change.recommendation: Split into 'transport hardware/waveforms/SATCOM' (capital-intensive, prime and SpaceX dominated) and 'network orchestration/PACE/transport-agnostic routing software'.
change.why: Software-only entrants (NetAgility-type, mesh sync) can play in the second; not in the first.

change.recommendation: Add 'MLOps for classified/edge and model assurance' as the startup-accessible sub-slice; keep hardware kits with edge PED.
change.why: Striveworks and SciTec wins indicate MLOps/fusion algorithms are procured separately from platforms.

added_segments: Platform app ecosystem and developer tooling (apps on Maven/Lattice/Foundry, SDK integrations, marketplaces)
Test, evaluation, instrumentation and EW/threat emulation for C2 experimentation (Ivy Sting cadence, DASH, GIDE X, NTC instrumentation)
Assessment/BDA and effects analytics (weakest step in chain, no incumbents found)
Human-machine teaming and decision support (explicit DAF DASH focus; cognitive load is an Army NGC2 metric)
C2 resilience/counter-C2 and cyber for C2 stacks (Army now names its portfolio 'Command and Control/Counter Command and Control')
